summary.one_liner: Lazygit is a terminal UI for running common git operations such as staging hunks, interactive rebasing, cherry-picking, and bisecting without memorizing git commands.
summary.what_it_does: It provides a keyboard-driven terminal interface over git. You can stage whole hunks or individual lines, and use a line-by-line mode with a range selection. It supports interactive rebase (squash, fixup, drop, edit, and move commits) as well as one-off actions on single commits. Other features include cherry-pick, git bisect marking, amending an old commit with staged changes, creating worktrees from branches, and building custom patches to move changes between commits. It also has undo and redo based on the reflog, a commit graph view, a mode for comparing two commits, and optional GitHub pull request display via the gh tool. Custom commands and Gitflow support are also mentioned.
use_cases: stage individual lines or hunks of a file
interactively rebase or squash commits without editing a TODO file
undo a git mistake using the reflog
manage git worktrees for several branches at once
review and compare two commits in a terminal
how_to_run: git clone the repository, cd lazygit, go install
stack: gh (optional, for GitHub pull request display)
notable: Line-by-line and hunk staging with a split diff view
Undo and redo of commit and branch actions via the reflog
Custom patches to move hunks into new commits (rebase magic)
Custom commands and custom diff renderers
Gitflow support through git-flow-next or Gitflow
caveats: Undo does not cover working tree changes or stashes, only commits and branches
GitHub PR display requires the gh tool and gh auth login; GitHub Enterprise needs extra configuration
Many packaged versions are maintained by third parties and may lag behind upstream
